reel: Skylab falls on Esperance, Western Australia (July 1979): NASA's A$400 littering fine, paid 30 years later by a California radio audience
status: 4 NASA originals (3 colour orbit/launch photos + 1 film segment cut from NASA's own 1973 documentary) and 4 Wikimedia Commons files downloaded; SHA1 of every Commons file matches the Commons API. Colour opener is the famous SL4-143-4706 overhead view of Skylab with the gold parasol sunshade. No rights-clear photo of the 2009 cheque, of Scott Barley, of Stan Thornton, or of the original 1979 recovery scenes was found (those are press/wire photos). No PD map of the re-entry track found at usable resolution.

rejected.what: File:Balladonia Museum, Western Australia - Skylab wreckage 01.jpg and 02.jpg (Chuq, CC BY-SA 4.0)
rejected.why: Downloaded, viewed, then deleted: Bahnfrend's photos of the same Balladonia roadhouse museum (Balladonia Museum, 2017 (06).jpg) describe the display as 'replica Skylab debris'; the panels (UNITED STATES lettering, AIRLOCK/DANGER decals, clean paint, clean cut edges) look fabricated. Would mislead as real wreckage. History.com does say the Balladonia Museum houses 'a pair of large pieces of sheet metal'; real-vs-replica unresolved, so excluded.

assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR. The famous overhead view of the complete Skylab cluster against a cloud-covered Earth, taken from the Skylab 4 command module on 8 Feb 1974 during the final fly-around. Gold parasol sunshade over the workshop, four-wing ATM solar array, one surviving workshop solar wing on the right, the missing left wing, black limb of space at the top.
assets.best_segments: THE OPENER. Near-square; for 9:16 crop x 1150-3250 at full height (station centred, Earth limb top-right). Slow push-in on the gold parasol for the first 2 s; later re-use with a 'falls to Earth' tilt-down.

assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR, highest resolution. Close-up of Skylab from the Skylab 3 command module before docking, 28 July 1973; hand-held Hasselblad on Ektachrome. Shows the single surviving workshop solar wing and the parasol over the bare workshop.
assets.best_segments: Alternate opener or second beat ('77 tonnes of space station'). Huge file: can crop to a tight 9:16 on the workshop cylinder without loss.

assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR. Skylab as the first crew found it in May 1973: micrometeoroid shield gone, bare gold-foil workshop, one solar wing torn off, the other jammed by a strap. Sets up 'damaged from day one'.
assets.best_segments: Short beat for the station's troubled history, or skip if the reel is only about the fall.

assets.license_note: Derived file: seconds 92-124 of the 22 min 43 s NASA documentary (1080p Commons transfer, SHA1 b1deb0a769e9f6f6009b794e677bdc98aec1c126), re-encoded to H.264 mp4. Film narration/music is NASA's and PD; mute it and use our own VO.
assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR 16mm film: 0-4 s pad close-up and ignition fireball; 4-22 s the Saturn V climbing on a long exhaust plume through haze; 22-32 s tracking shots of the stack with the S-II stage and Skylab shroud. Vintage grain and faded colour.
assets.best_segments: Use 2-10 s (ignition to climb) as the 'launched 14 May 1973' beat; 23-30 s (close tracking shot) for a punchier cut. Centre-crop to 9:16 keeps the rocket.

assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR. A real recovered piece: one of Skylab's six oxygen tanks, a shredded fibreglass-wound cylinder about 2 m long, in a glass case at the US Space & Rocket Center, Huntsville. The placard (readable when zoomed) says 'Skylab O2 Tank Fragment ... one of six that provided breathable air to the crew in the Orbital Workshop (OWS). This piece was recovered near Esperance, Australia' and captions a 1979 photo of a US Customs official inspecting it at San Francisco International Airport.
assets.best_segments: 'This is what came down' beat. Crop out the placard inset (unlicensed press photo): 9:16 on the tank body x 600-2050. Slow drift along the frayed fibres.

assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR, native portrait. The 'SKYLAB 1979' model-monument on a concrete plinth outside the Esperance Museum, WA. The plaque reads: 'It completed 34,981 orbits of Earth before it came crashing to Earth over Esperance in the early hours of July 12th 1979 ... spreading all the way to Balladonia and beyond.' NOTE: the plaque misprints the launch date as '24th May 1973' (it was 14 May); do not show that line.
assets.best_segments: 'The town that fined NASA' beat; full 9:16 with no crop. Zoom the plaque for '34,981 orbits'.

assets.credit_line: Document: Archives New Zealand, CC BY-SA 2.0 (Ministry of Civil Defence letter CD 120/6, 19 June 1979)
assets.what_it_shows: COLOUR scan of a typed two-page primary document: NZ Ministry of Civil Defence letter of 19 June 1979, 'SKYLAB RE-ENTRY ACTIVITY': re-entry expected 7-25 July; 'approximately 500 pieces capable of causing injury'; '2 weigh over 1770kg'; 'the chances of anyone, anywhere in the world being hit are 1 in 150; the chances of any one person being hit are 1 in 600,000,000,000'; 'civil defence can go back to bed'.
assets.best_segments: Document beat for 'the world braced': crop 9:16 on the left page (x 60-1000) and push in on the '1 in 150' paragraph.
